ORAL JUDGMENT (PER- A.S. GADKARI, J.):-
1) By the present Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the Petitioner, victim in C.R. No.399 of 2019, registered with Malad ssm 246-wp646.2021.doc Police Station, Mumbai, dated 24th September, 2019 under Sections 409 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
has prayed for transfer of the said investigation to any other Police Station and/or any other Senior Rishab S/O Dinesh Halwai vs The State Of Maharashtra on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72595664/
1 Officer of the Respondent Police Station with a direction to carry out further investigation in the interest of justice.
2) Record indicates that, by an Order dated 22 nd February, 2023, present Petition is admitted.
Learned APP had appeared at the time of admitting the Petition.
Respondent till date has not filed reply in opposition to the Petition and/or any other response to the Petition.
Today also, learned APP seeks time to take instructions.

2.1) We are unable to accept the request of the learned APP to grant him an adjournment, as after the admission of the Petition, the Respondent has not bothered to file response or to give instructions to the learned APP and therefore under the law, a safe inference can be drawn that the Respondent has no objection for grant of prayer clause (a) of the Petition.
3) In view of the above, Petition is allowed in terms of prayer clause (a).
4) We direct the Deputy Commissioner of Police having territorial jurisdiction over the Malad Police Station, Mumbai to transfer the investigation of the said crime to the other police officer not below the rank of Senior Police Inspector and to carry further investigation, as the earlier Investigating Officer has already filed charge-sheet.

ssm 246-wp646.2021.d  5) The new Investigating Officer so appointed, shall take into consideration various communications addressed by the Petitioner to the Senior Police Inspector,
Malad Police Station, Mumbai which are annexed to the Petition.
6) Rule is made absolute in the above terms.
( DR. NEELA GOKHALE, J.) (A.S. GADKARI, J.)
